ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, there are 5 000 small balls each with mass m. They are connected in sequence with light ropes of equal length, then their left end is fixed to the ceiling with a thin rope, and a horizontal force is applied at the right end to make all the small balls stationary. If the angle between the thin rope connected to the ceiling and the horizontal direction is 45°, then the tangent value of the angle α between the light rope between the 2011th small ball and the 2012th small ball and the horizontal direction is equal to (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, there are 5000 small balls each with mass m. They are connected in sequence with light ropes of equal length, then their left end is fixed to the ceiling with a thin rope, and a horizontal force is applied at the right end to make all the small balls stationary. If the angle between the thin rope connected to the ceiling and the horizontal direction is 45°, find the tangent value of the angle α between the light rope between the 2011th small ball and the 2012th small ball and the horizontal direction.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the upper left of the figure is the ceiling. The thin rope at the left end connects obliquely downward to the right from the ceiling to the 1st small ball, and the figure marks that the angle between this thin rope and the horizontal direction is 45°. Many small balls are connected in sequence by light ropes along a sagging chain-like curve, and the figure marks the 1st, 2nd, 2011th, 2012th, and 4998th, 4999th, 5000th small balls. The far right end is subjected to an external force F horizontally to the right at the 5000th small ball, and the whole system is stationary. Then reason: Take all 5000 small balls as a whole for force analysis. The whole is subjected to the total gravity 5000mg downward, the horizontal pulling force F at the right end to the right, and the tension of the thin rope at the left end from the ceiling along the direction of the thin rope. Since the thin rope at the left end makes an angle of 45° with the horizontal direction, its vertical component and horizontal component are equal in magnitude. In equilibrium, the vertical component of the left-end tension balances 5000mg, and the horizontal component balances F, so tan45° = 5000mg/F. Because tan45°=1, obtain F=5000mg. It is required to find the angle α between the light rope between the 2011th small ball and the 2012th small ball and the horizontal direction. Cut out the part on the right side of this light rope, namely the 2012th to the 5000th small balls, with a total of 5000−2011=2989 small balls, and the total gravity is 2989mg; it is still subjected to the horizontal pulling force F at the far right end to the right. The tension of the light rope at this section must provide a leftward horizontal component F and an upward vertical component 2989mg, therefore the inclination angle of this light rope relative to the horizontal direction satisfies tanα = vertical component/horizontal component = 2989mg/F = 2989mg/(5000mg)=2989/5000.
